narr: Extremely heavy rainfall associated with the remnants of Hurricane Ida overspread southern Connecticut during the evening of September 1 and continued through the early morning hours of September 2. Rainfall totals ranged from 5-8+ inches across much of the region, with much of that rain falling in just a few hours. This resulted in not only widespread flash flooding but also extensive river flooding. The ASOS at Bridgeport Airport recorded 5.59 inches of rain. A CoCoRaHS observer near Stamford recorded 8.10 inches of rain, while another in Uncasville reported 8.58 inches. Broadcast media reported 8.37 and 8.90 inches in Clinton and near Madison, respectively.
ev: The entire ground floor of an apartment building in New Haven was flooded.
Fairfield Police reported numerous flooded streets and road closures across town.
The intersection of Cove Road and Seaside Avenue in Darien was closed due to flooding.
Multiple cars were stranded in flood waters in Stamford with water rescues ongoing.
Multiple cars were stranded in flood waters on I-95 near Bridgeport with water above the car doors.
The West Haven Police closed Campbell Avenue in West Haven due to flooding.
Heavy rain and flash flooding resulted in uninsured damages of $50,266 across Middlesex County.
Heavy rain and flash flooding resulted in uninsured damages of $706,239 across New London County.

The Quinnipiac River at Wallingford rose above its minor flood stage of 10.0 feet at 3:15am EDT September 2nd. The river ultimately crested at a height of 11.25 feet at 6:15am EDT and 7:45am EDT before falling back below flood stage by 9:00am EDT.

Power had to be turned off to numerous homes throughout Norwich for safety due to flooded basements. In addition, the Comfort Inn and Suites on Otrobando Avenue had to be evacuated due to more than 5 feet of water in the basement of the hotel. Three apartments in Mohegan Commons on East Baltic Street were flooded and uninhabitable.
Significant flooding was reported into the first floors of multiple dorms at Yale University in New Haven.
Several streets were impassible in Meriden due to significant flash flooding.
A car was partially submerged in flood waters on Mill Street near State Street in Meriden. Mill Street was closed due to heavy flooding.
Several roads were closed due to flooding in Waterford including Route 85 at the I-95 overpass, Gardiners Wood Road, and Old Colchester Road at I-395.
Heavy rain and flash flooding resulted in uninsured damages of $5,112,636 across Fairfield County.
